name: social ease
description: Being comfortable enough with your social skills to interact socially with unfamiliar people and larger groups.
perceptions: I don't know this person or group.
I'm confident in my social skills.
examples: Comfortable in a big noisy party with strangers.

guidance.description: If you want to improve a sense of social ease, see guidance for 'shyness'.

comparisons.description: 'Social comfort' is about the immediate social situation while 'social ease' is a general confidence in social skills. Someone can be generally comfortable, but feel uncomfortable in a particular situation.

Generally, extroverted people are stimulated by being around people and are at ease around crowds. However, there may be scenarios where a person normally at ease becomes more shy. Examples may include meeting celebrities, meeting with foreigners, or giving an important presentation.
A shy person is likely afraid of social failure. A person at ease socially is not.

commentaries.quote: People may forget what you said, but they will never forget how you made them feel.
You can make more friends in two months by becoming interested in other people than you can in two years by trying to get other people interested in you.
Communication is merely an exchange of information, but connection is an exchange of our humanity.
Since you cannot do good to all, you are to pay special attention to those who, by the accidents of time, or place, or circumstances, are brought into closer connection with you.
The less you speak, the more you will hear.
